opus.name: GMB-opus-Maestro Otto Kettle
opus.description: A big, booming, theatrical baritone that sounds like a man in his mid-forties. Rich and resonant with a little warm gravel at the edges, built to fill a concert hall or a packed hockey barn. His delivery works like a crescendo: he can drop to a hushed, conspiratorial whisper and then swell into a full-chested roar on the big word. Quick, punchy pacing with dramatic pauses before reveals. Playful and gleeful, never mean, with a hearty rolling laugh. Light East Coast Canadian warmth in the vowels, nothing exaggerated.

deepseek.name: GMB-deepseek-Randy Saucer Kulyk
deepseek.description: Baritone with a dry, gravelly warmth, like twenty winters spent yelling "again" over bantam practice in a cold rink. Northeast Alberta farm-country accent — flat prairie vowels, an easy "eh" on the end of a question, the odd dropped "g" when he's loose, never a put-on. Humming, unhurried pace; he lets a deadpan line hang in the silence a beat before the laugh. Sounds late thirties. Steady and low; the loud comes from the moment, not the man.

fugu.description: East-central Alberta farm-and-oilpatch accent: flat prairie vowels, hard R's, the odd sentence tipping up into a little "eh". Low baritone sitting close to bass, with a gravelly rasp from thirty winters of cold arena air. Sounds mid-to-late fifties. Unhurried pace — short sentences, a beat of silence before the punchline, each word set down like he's laying it on a table. Warm underneath, never sharp, with a creak at the bottom of the register when he's amused.
fugu.chosen_reason: design candidate attempt 1 preview 0 of 1: plain-read F0 163.6 Hz vs tenor band 125-165 (off 0.0 st); nearest cast voice fable 0.706; preview lift 6.89, real v3 lift 11.13; WER 0.17

spec.signature_quality: slow, weathered old-timer's voice with a low creak
spec.diverged: age mid-to-late fifties -> late 60s; texture creaky/weathered (the card's own 'creak at the bottom of the register') instead of gravelly: the card's mid-50s gravelly low baritone collided with qwen (speaker similarity 0.82-0.84 on all six previews of 2026-09-27); register tenor (card: low baritone near bass): a thin, creaky late-60s old-timer (~160 Hz); every lower design either collided with qwen, failed the accent check, or would not shout

casting.design_prompt: Native Canadian English with a clear, natural rural east-central Alberta (Canadian prairie) accent, never a caricature. Male, late 60s. Baritone speaking voice with a creaky, weathered, warm texture. Slow, weathered old-timer's voice with a creak. Natural speaking voice with a wide dynamic range: relaxed and conversational at rest, capable of a full, powerful shout. Clear studio recording.

accent.target: a rural Alberta / Canadian prairie accent
accent.method: pairwise vs a General American reference voice reading the same words, both orders

orders.why: Speaker A displays the authentic cadence, vowel quality (especially in words like 'ice' and 'sheet'), and relaxed drawl typical of older rural Western Canadian/prairie speech, whereas Speaker B has a polished, standard North American announ

Speaker B exhibits clear Canadian raising on the diphthongs before voiceless consonants, most notably in 'county' and 'ice'. The prosody, vowel qualities, and overall cadence are highly characteristic of an older rural Western Canadian/prai

sol.name: GMB-sol-Sol Vant
sol.description: A ringing lower-mid voice with a bright, brassy edge and the carrying power to cut through a packed arena. Mid-thirties impression; fast, rhythmic setup, sudden booming emphasis, then a grinning pause before the punch line. Slightly grainy when yelling a pick, crisp and warm when explaining a move. Light northern Canadian cadence, never an exaggerated accent. Excitable without losing control: every announcement sounds like the puck just hit the back bar.
sol.chosen_reason: design candidate attempt 1 preview 0 of 3: plain-read F0 135.5 Hz vs high baritone band 110-145 (off 0.0 st); nearest cast voice fugu 0.774; [excited] lift 7.07; WER 0.03

casting.design_prompt: Male, mid-thirties. Light, high baritone speaking voice with a brassy, ringing, bright texture. Bright brassy ring. Light northern Canadian, nothing exaggerated. Natural, conversational delivery at a relaxed volume. Clear studio recording.
